utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are continuing cross-examination with Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mehinovic, good afternoon. I introduced myself yesterday and we started this cross-examination, and I would like to continue from where we stopped yesterday. I only have a few more questions that have to do with April 17th, 1992. I would like to clarify several minor things. We were talking about the group of people that went towards Donja Mahala and afterwards returned. They were dressed in civilian clothes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And they were armed? We could say that these were people -- actually, these people were armed civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to hear something about your impressions, keeping in mind that Ibrahim Salkic had this walkie-talkie, as you said, and he talked -- spoke on it with Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic. Was Ibrahim Salkic the leader of this group? Was that your impression?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have one further question about this. At the very end, when you came to the yard of this Carrington building, this is a building with apartments and it has a huge yard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So including these 20 people that went towards the school and those who joined you later, how many people were there all together?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It might have been 20 of the first group and four that joined us later, so maybe around 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. I'm not going to insist on that number. After this event, you returned home; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you stayed home that whole day?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what time it was when you returned home, approximately, if you could remember, please.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might have been around 9.00, 9.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you say around 9.30. Okay. So you remained home the whole day?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And after that, so tomorrow, the day after, you had this event of gathering weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So that happened on the 18th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: According to what you testified on before, you said that there was an armoured vehicle that was driving along the street and that there was a loudspeaker calling people to surrender arms.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not an armoured vehicle. It was a jeep, and a jeep is not an armoured vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. It might be the case that I misunderstood. But if I read the transcript correctly - and this is the unofficial transcript - you were talking about an armoured vehicle. You also mentioned a jeep later that had a loudspeaker, but -- so what you're saying is that this was not an armoured vehicle the first time around?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This voice that you heard through the loudspeakers and that was calling people to surrender weapons, was this a voice that belonged to Ibrahim Salkic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Pasaga Tihic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did that voice belong to him?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Then in your statement you mentioned Dragan Borojevic.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He came to your house, and you knew this Dragan Borojevic from before. He was an engineer, one of the directors of Mebos

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was my director when I used to work there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He was dressed in a grey-green uniform, a uniform belonging to the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. He was wearing a uniform of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise him immediately?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Without any problems whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't notice that maybe he had a black colour on his face?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Borojevic and these other soldiers that came, did they enter your house or not?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were standing on the staircase.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So I assume that they did not go through your house and look through it.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Neither did they search your brother's house? I would say this is really the same house, your and your brother's house, just divided in two parts?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So they did not search your brother's house either?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: They also didn't search any of the houses of your neighbours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, okay. If you don't know, we'll move on. Let's now move on to the events that you also described, this meeting that happened in front of Buducnost factory. You said that at that meeting Jovo Savic was talking.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You knew Jovo Savic from before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He worked in the military command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was deputy commander of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From what you remember, do you know that Jovo Savic had a white armband?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that he had that old uniform, the old JNA uniform, grey-green uniform?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he had that uniform on, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Apart from Jovo Savic, were there any other soldiers there? Could you remember that, please?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, as you said, the loudspeaker, it was said over the loudspeaker that everybody who had uniforms should come in front of Buducnost factory.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So there was a number of people gathered there, you said 40, 50?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So there were Serbs there as well?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So Jovo Savic said to those who gathered there that those who want to could join the 4th Detachment and get weapons and those who do not want to join the 4th Detachment should return their uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't understand it well. We all had to return the uniforms, but whoever wanted to -- whoever wanted to could get help and protection from Jovo Savic, and then Jovo Savic said that they should go to Cafe AS, that they would get the answer and that they would get security.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, which building is opposite the Cafe AS? Is Sit there?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mladost is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you know of this, but I will ask you anyway. Do you know that this was the location where the command of the 4th Detachment was located?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I understood that people who wanted protection, they were invited to join the JNA and that that, in principle, would mean that they were working on their own protection.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I wasn't aware of it and I did not understand that in such a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that shortly after this event -- let me just ask you one more question. This uniform that you were told to return, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's why I came there. I came to return it. I didn't go there to look at anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you returned the uniform?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To whom?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned it to Jovo Savic, to the person that called me to get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, sir. I wasn't there and I don't know all the details, and that's why I'm asking you questions.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that afterwards you were sent to dig trenches in Pisari. If you could please remember the names that worked with you together, that would be very helpful.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a little bit hard right now to remember everybody who was there. For example, Sead Causevic

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was Dagovic Safet there?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. If you cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was to go there to work and not to meet other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After digging these trenches in Pisari, you said that you were building bunkers and digging trenches on the embankment in the very city of Samac.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These bunkers that were built, could you please explain to me the following: From the very -- from where the very last homes were to the place where the bunkers were built, how far are these two locations from the bunker to the houses?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might have been not even more than ten metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So the bunkers were practically on the very border of this town?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please also tell me approximately what was the distance from these bunkers to the road?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, maybe about 150 to 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You were also talking about sniper fire. The sniper fire was coming from the direction of Prud?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. There was sniper fire, but from what direction, I have no idea, because this part is the very end of the town, where the River Bosna flows into Sava. On the right-hand side was Croatia and on the left-hand side was the village of Prud.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So the sniper fire could have come both from Prud or from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So these bunkers, this part of Samac where they were being built, during the war this part of town was the one that was shelled the most and also destroyed the most?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would like to move on to the very day of May 27th, when you were arrested. When the policemen came to your home, could you please tell me what time it was?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just to clear things up, was this 4.00 in the morning or 4.00 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You already said who these policemen were. They took you to the SUP building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So when you arrived in the SUP building, the officer on duty started handling you and you said that you had to give him all the documents and shoelaces and everything else?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you were arrested, meaning in May, at that time the police chief was Stevan Todorovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this the same Stevan Todorovic that later beat you in the police station? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you were brought to the police station around 4.00. I'm assuming that you actually arrived at the police station very shortly after you were arrested, because it's very close. From the time that you were brought to the police station to Goran's arrival - and this Goran was the bodyguard of Stevan Todorovic - how much time passed?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This might have been about half an hour later, right after I was taken into the reception room.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did Goran come alone or not?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And he then told you to, in Cyrillic, write a statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you answer anything to him at that time?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything else?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He left the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At that point he did not beat you up?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, my colleague Lukic already asked you about the statement that you gave to the Prosecutor on April 23rd, 1998, and I think I have reason to ask you some further questions about that. You said that you stand by this statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Related to these events, I'm going to read out to you what you said at that time.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean in the SUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. I mean what you said to the Prosecutors of The Hague Tribunal, the statement that you made in 1998: "At the entrance they told me to empty my pockets and take off my watch, before they took me to one of the reception rooms. Stevo Todorovic entered the room with his bodyguard Goran, last name unknown. Goran gave me a piece of paper and told me to write a confession what I was doing before the war broke out. I was supposed to write what kind of weapon I had, who I shot, and who was the head of SDA. I told them that I had nothing to write, and then they started to beat me with a baseball bat. They beat me about an hour and then they left. They said that they would be back in about an hour and a half and that they wanted to see a written confession in Cyrillic." Mr. Mehinovic, based on your decision -- based on your statement that you gave to the Tribunal, you are very well aware that there are some differences. First of all, you said that Stevan Todorovic came together with his bodyguard Goran; second, that they told you to write the statement, and you said you had nothing to write; and third, that they then beat you for an hour with a baseball bat. What is true: What you said then or what you said today?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was -- at the time when I was giving my statement, I did not think that it was important to give all the details to such an extent as you are asking me of today. I just gave -- said what was happening, and actually, they did start beating me after the gentleman left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So there are quite a few details in your statement. I'm asking you again: Which statement is true, the statement you gave to the Tribunal or the statement you gave today? This is a very simple question.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand you. Which statement do you mean, today?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The statement that you gave today in front of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement that I gave today in front of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course, I'm not objecting to this particular line of questioning. I am, however, going to put in an objection to the particular phrase that Mr. Lazarevic is using. We've already said that this statement was not reread to the witness, et cetera. He didn't adopt it at the time. If he wants to ask witness which is a more accurate recording of what happened at the time, what is recorded by the investigators in that statement or what he said to the Tribunal, it's one thing, but he keeps asking which one is true, and that implies that Mr. Mehinovic at some time deliberately has chosen to lie. I think he should either ask Mr. Mehinovic whether he lied to investigators or lied to the Tribunal or whether one recording of his statement is -- which version is more accurate according to his memory. So as I said, it's the line of questioning I understand, and of course it's permissible, but the implication about whether or not Mr. Mehinovic was deliberately telling the truth or not is something that I would object to, unless counsel wants to deliberately put that allegation to the witness: Did you at one stage lie to either the Tribunal or to the investigators about what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure, Mr. Lazarevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I can reply. First of all, my colleague Mr. Lukic has already made a ground for this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We are fully aware also that this statement was not signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But he already asked this witness if this statement was read to him when he arrived here, and he answered that it was. And he again asked him: Do you still stand by this statement? And he said he did. So I do believe that I'm entitled to use the word "statement," since it was somehow authorised by the witness that this is what he said and that he still stands on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic. The Trial Chamber doesn't see anything wrong with your line of questioning. Of course, the witness -- if the witness wants to explain as to the truthfulness of either of the statements, he can go ahead and do so. I'm sure he's understanding the language being used.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will definitely allow the witness to say everything he wishes to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After this event about which you testified, when Goran gave you that piece of paper, how much time elapsed before Nijaz Alatovic and the other three men you mentioned, Brica and the others, turned up?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened very quickly, after about ten minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: According to what you are saying now, you had not been beaten by Stevan Todorovic and the others at that point.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You testified here that one of the policemen arrived, called out Nijaz Alatovic's name, and said that Simo Zaric was expecting him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This was one of the policemen who arrived in that room where the five of you were?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What time was it, approximately, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. We didn't have a watch. I didn't have a watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I don't want to irritate the Prosecutor by calling it your statement, but in this informal statement you made, you said the following in connection with this: "At about 1715 hours, Simo Zaric arrived and called out Nijaz Alatovic's name." So was it Simo Zaric who arrived and called out his name or was it a policeman who arrived and called out Nijaz Alatovic's name?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I said it was a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After this -- bear with me for a moment, please. -- Nijaz Alatovic left, the others also left, and you were left on your own; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I would like the assistance of the usher, because I would like to show to the witness a photograph, it bears the number P14, photograph number 43. It was already used during this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Has this already --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I could just check if this is the same one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The usher will show him the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you have already seen this photograph. You pointed out the room where you were; is that correct, and you said it was the room practically next to this tree which can be seen in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, looking at this this way, in relation to the door, do you see the entrance to the SUP?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you point it out so that others can see it.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So it was the first room to the left of the entrance?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was the second room to the left of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I correct myself. So it was the second room to the left of the entrance?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...photograph the witness indicated second window left from the main entrance of the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't need this photograph any more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, the room where you were has only one window, looking out on the street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And this room has only one entrance?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was a door through which you entered and there was another door leading into another room.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was referring to the entrance to that room.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was only one entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you entered that room, was there any furniture in it, any cupboards or ...

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only a table under the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Only a table under the window. That door - I'm referring to the entrance leading into the room, the door through which one entered the room, it was an ordinary wooden door?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't a cell with bars; it was just a normal wooden door?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the first day after your arrest, you didn't leave the room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You didn't go out into the corridor or into a neighbouring room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not on that first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And Simo Zaric did not enter the room where you were; he didn't open the door and go in?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I am again referring to the informal statement which you made to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal. There you said: "I was the only one left in the room when he came. Simo Zaric himself came to fetch me, with his bodyguard and another policeman." You see for yourself that this is different from your testimony here before the Court. Did Simo Zaric enter the room with, as you said, his bodyguard, or didn't he?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This may have been a misunderstanding about the name but not about what happened, because I said on several occasions that Stevan Todorovic had his own bodyguard, and that was a man whom I knew. I never said that Simo Zaric had a bodyguard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I wanted to clarify, sir, because that is how I have been instructed. So what you said then actually referred to Stevan Todorovic and his bodyguard?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Objection. Now the counsel is using the statement, and it's not -- I don't mind counsel calling it a statement as long as everybody understands the context, and my original objection was about truth, but on this occasion he's using the statement improperly. The statement never says that Simo Zaric entered the room, which is what Defence counsel has said. It says Simo Zaric came to me personally with his bodyguard and a police officer." Now the witness is explaining that he didn't say -- that he didn't mean that Simo Zaric had a bodyguard, it was a police officer. When he's talking about the bodyguard, maybe he means Stevan Todorovic, but not about -- now he has a completely different incident coming into the room and it stems back from putting to the witness that he said in his statement that Simo Zaric entered the room and it does not say in the statement that Simo Zaric entered the room. It says, "Simo Zaric came to me personally. He told the bodyguard and the police officer they should beat me until I confess. They did not beat me and left." Now, if he wants to ask about it and he wants to ask about the statement and put so much reliance on it, then he must put the words of the statement to the witness and not try to imply other meanings out of the words and therefore in his -- you know, from -- by counsel himself trying to conflaite two incidents without the witness knowing the full facts. I apologise to the interpreters. I've just seen my order to slow down for the record. I know I repetitively do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's important to slow down for the record to be correct. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe I read exactly what is stated in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's what I was wondering about. Maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't implicating anything. I was just reading in B/C/S what is said here in the statement. And for -- just to clarify all this. I will read this again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I was the last one and alone in the room when he came. Simo Zaric came to me personally with his bodyguard and a police officer. He told the bodyguard and the police officer that they should beat me until I confessed. They did not beat me, and left." [In English] And after I read this, the witness stated that it is obviously some confusion and that he referred probably to Stevan Todorovic because he's the one who had bodyguard because -- well, maybe I will ask this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, Simo Zaric did not have a bodyguard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I know. I never saw him with one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Simo Zaric did not enter the room and tell two other men who were either bodyguards or police officers, he did not enter the room and say that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not in my room at all on the first day, nor did he say anything like that. There was Goran, Tadic, Zakasu [phoen]. Those were the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Their names have been mentioned here on several occasions and not just in connection with you.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that after finishing the conversation with those four, because I was standing in the left-hand corner near the door - I could see the whole corridor - Simo Zaric gave a sign. He gave an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We shall arrive at that. We'll come to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would only like to ask that it be clarified with the witness what it says in line 19. It says there was "Goran, Tadic, and there are two empty spaces." So when he said Tadic, what? Which Tadic was he referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, when you said Tadic, which Tadic did you mean?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to Goran?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is that the person called Goran Tadic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't understand you. I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will try --

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a mistake. Goran was the bodyguard of Stevan Todorovic, but what is in the record, I don't know how it was taken down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can clear that with the witness, Counsel, by asking him whether among the people who were in the room there was anybody called by this name, Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you have heard the judge. Among the people who arrived together with Stevan and entered the room, was there someone named Tadic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no personal knowledge of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us clear this up even further. At the moment we're interested in Mr. Miroslav Tadic. Did he enter the room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't there at all while I was in the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That was what my colleague was concerned about, and I had to clear this up. You said during your examination by the Prosecution that you were sitting in the left-hand corner of the room. That's on page 30 of your informal statement.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Standing, then. As the room has four corners, tell me: When you say "the left-hand corner," is it looking from the door towards the window or looking from the window towards the door?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The left-hand corner is looking from the door -- looking at the window and at the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the left-hand corner," were you near the window or near the door?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you were facing the door and you were to the left of the door?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, when you testified, we called our investigators and they went to the SUP building and saw the room where you said you had been incarcerated, they opened the door a little, a little more, a little wider, but in whatever way they opened the door, they could not see that side of the corridor where the staircase is and the desk where the duty officer sat. Do you still say that you saw Mr. Zaric coming down the stairs?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say I saw Mr. Zaric coming down the stairs. What I said was that I saw him in the corridor, with the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But sir, our investigators went on looking, and this is in view of the angle at which the door opens on quite the opposite side from what you say. You could not have seen that part of the corridor from that room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, could you tell us which way the door swings?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the right side --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Does it go this way or does it go to that way?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, first of all I first must apologise. I don't want to be considered not ready for this trial, but this was actually the first time that we heard where was the exact room where this witness was kept, and it was yesterday, the day before yesterday. And also, this was the first time that we hear stated about his position in that space. So we didn't -- we were not in position to make photographs, and I will definitely do that in due course, to show the way the door opens and everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At this time, I just want to say that what -- what are the observations of our investigators on field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Just one other question. As we all know, properties get renovated, door jambs can change. Having someone look at the way a door swings now in 2002 might not be the same way the door was swinging in 1992, 1993. So that's I think something else to take into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm fully aware of that fact and we will have all this in consideration when approaching this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mehinovic, you said that Nijaz Alatovic went to be interrogated and after that you saw him leaving the SUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You were not present when he had his interview?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You don't even know whether this interview actually took place?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the same goes for the other three: You don't actually know whether they even saw Zaric. These are simply assumptions. And then you saw them leaving the SUP. So this is an assumption, not something you have personal knowledge of?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it from the guards. The guards called them out, their names out, one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But you were not present when this was going on?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was in the room when the guard was calling out their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But after they left the room, you don't know what really happened?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me put one more question to you in connection with this. You said you knew Nijaz Alatovic. Did you ever meet him afterwards?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You did not have an opportunity to talk to him?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more point I would like to ask you about, and it refers to an incident you mentioned in your statement made to this Tribunal, and it concerns a certain Dadan. You know what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to clarify who this person is, is this Aladin Jakupovic, known as Dadi, a big, strong man, who was a bouncer in a disco who had a BMW car and a motorcycle? Is that the man?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So we are referring to the same person. According to what you said before this Tribunal, you assume that this person was killed in the Territorial Defence building when you were already incarcerated in the SUP and that this happened at about 5.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in connection with this event, I don't wish to deny that Dadan died, but from several sources, including sources opened up to us by the Prosecution and sources in the books, I'm speaking of the book by Dragan Lukac "Samac, the camp town," on page 25 [As interpreted], and from some other sources, we learnt that this unfortunate Aladin, known as Dadan, was killed on the 15th of May, in Obudovac, which is 12 days before you were detained and in a completely different place from the Territorial Defence building. That is why I am asking you now whether you know anything about this or whether it is just hearsay, something you repeated before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had heard this from Mirsad Kikic, who cleaned the corridors. That's the first thing. It could have been around 8.00. And his aunt was at the door of the TO, looking for her nephew. And to tell you the truth, I don't know who killed him or where. I just said that at that time this is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you don't really know?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've told you. I think you have it in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one thing in the transcript, because when I quoted Samac, the camp town, I said on page 75, and here it is stated on page 25. It is page 24, line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. You are talking about the book -- the page in the book?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the book of Dragan Lukac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it should be page -- the correct page is page what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the correct page is page 75.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Mehinovic. My name is Slobodan Zecevic and I will put a few questions to you in connection with only one matter, because my colleagues have, for the most part, covered all my other questions. Mr. Mehinovic, you were detained on the 27th of May, at around 1600 hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were brought to the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You showed us a few moments ago, in response to my colleague's question, what room you were in.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The second door to the left of the door?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The entrance door?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In that room, if I remember your statement correctly, you said you spent about seven days.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Six or seven. I can't be quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After that you were taken to another room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Where there were about 20 of you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me where this other room was? Was it in the same building?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at the entrance to the door, the first door to the left of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...Your Honours, at this time P14, photograph 43, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mehinovic -- thank you. Yes, I see you've got the pointer. So would you first show us the second room to the left of the door where you spent the first week.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is that the room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the room where you were transferred later, the first room next to the door?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're obviously confused by the tree. There are only two windows there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how many rooms -- would you first show us the entrance to the SUP building. Please be kind enough, sir. Is that the entrance?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: How many rooms are there to the left?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So when you, on the 27th of May, when you arrived in the SUP, you were put in the second room to the left?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the second room to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You spent seven days there and you were transferred to the first --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would counsel and witness please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- pausing between yourself and the witness, and the witness should also pause, wait a moment before starting to answer, otherwise the record won't be --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- won't make sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Tell me --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher, very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were in that room when you saw the beating of Mirsad Jasarevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So that was the first door, the one next to the entrance, the first room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said that in that room there were about 20 detainees together with you.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you remember at least the names of some of them, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pistoljevic Husein, Mirsad Srna, Kapetanovic, also known as Baca; Kovacevic; Zlatko Stanic; Kemal Bobic. I don't know. I think Stipo Crnjinski was also there, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, since it didn't enter the records: You said Husein Pistoljevic, and then Mirsad Srna; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Srna, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On Monday, while you were being -- during the investigation, on transcript page 7433, you said that all persons that were with you in that room saw the beating of Mr. Jasarevic, Mirsad.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "all persons," it would mean one of the persons that you listed now would have seen that beating?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could say that they did see it, because they were also being smacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the beating of Mirsad Jasarevic that was happening in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they saw it. Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At that time, you also said that there were four of them that were beating up Mirsad Jasarevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please list them once again, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Simic, Lugar, I think Tihi as well, and I cannot remember the fourth person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said during the examination on Monday that you think that the fourth person was an officer on duty, some person called Savo from Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible. I think there was a fourth person, and he was the officer on duty at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this Savo was the officer on duty?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were they all uniformed?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Savo as well?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did they all wear the same uniforms?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Savo was wearing a blue uniform. Everybody else had a camouflage uniform on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So he was wearing a police uniform?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This informal statement you gave to the Tribunal on April 23rd of 1998; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At that time you mentioned this incident with Mr. Jasarevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really remember, but if I would -- if I read it, I would know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is the only statement that you gave to the Prosecutor, is that correct -- to the investigators of the Prosecution, actually; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Milan Simic surrendered voluntarily to The Hague Tribunal in February of 1998? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read a portion of this statement about the same event. You said: "Milan Simic came a number of times to SUP to beat up prisoners." Then you said: "I remember he was beating Mirsad Jasarevic, called Bjelko. He took him out of the room where we were held, into the hallway. The doors were not closed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Objection. I don't know which version Mr. Zecevic is now reading from, but the version which I have in front of me, with an ERN number and which is the version disclosed and recorded by the investigators, does not say that "He was taken out of the room where we were held." It says: "I remember Mirsad Jasarevic, Bjelko, was beaten by him," meaning Milan Simic. "He took him out to the detention room to the hallway. The door was not closed, so I could see Milan Simic was beating him." He did not say he took him out of his detention room or that detention room where he was being held. He simply said he was taken out of a detention room. I think that's an important distinction to make, because this witness testified that Milan Simic had him brought up from the garage, to the detention cell, to the hallway, where he was beaten, and never said he was taken from the detention room where this particular witness was held, which is what Mr. Zecevic has read into the record, or at least is what I read coming up on the transcript

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, just very briefly. I am reading the Serbian translation, official translation, given to us by the Prosecutors, and this is the statement of Kemal Mehinovic in Serbian. It has the ERN number, this particular page, 00637087. But just for the purposes of not losing any more time, I will read from the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted this to -- to simplify it with the witness. It's perfectly the same to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to have to read this again, since there seem to be some unclear details regarding translation. [In English] "Milan Simic came several times to SUP to beat prisoners. I remember Mirsad Jasarevic, aka Bjelko, was beaten by him. He took him out of detention room to the hallway. The door was not closed, so I could see Milan Simic was beating him. He used police baton to beat him." [Interpretation] Do you remember saying this?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did, but I don't see any difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, when you said -- when you said "detention room," what room did you have in mind where Jasarevic came out of?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Detention room? I don't know I ever said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I read it to you.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said "the reception room," not any kind of detention room.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let's just clear this up. Are you now saying that Mr. Jasarevic was taken out of the reception room, into the hall, and beaten there?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So he was taken out of a room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Which room?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 you didn't say it was a garage.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's very possible. The more I'm being asked about this, the more I remember, because I'm thinking of more and more details.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that you talked about [as interpreted] the investigators in great detail; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say everything. Had I said everything, all the details would have been in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph - and I'm going to read this lest there be any unclear details. [In English] "Milan Simic had been arguing before the war, because Mirsad's sister was married to a colleague of Milan that he could not get along with."

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You did not repeat this during the investigation on Monday.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I just forgot it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me if you know the name of this gentleman, this colleague of Milan Simic, that he didn't agree with, who was married to Mirsad's sister?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please give us the name?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not authorised to give the name, because I was asked not to disclose it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would really need this name. Either maybe witness can write it down and then we put it under seal so it can be disclosed only to us, because we need it for our Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. You can -- the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Or we can go into private session, whichever way pleases the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it's faster to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I was notified by my colleagues that it's about time that we break, and I am going into another topic. Maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, although we still have I think a minute and a half. We can take our break and resume at 1615 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We continue with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mehinovic, could you please tell me the following: In your statement, this informal statement that you gave to the investigators of the Prosecutor on April 23rd, 1998, you didn't mention the incident that had to do with Nikola Vukovic that you described in some detail on Monday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Maybe the counsel could be more clear about which incident, because I believe that Mr. Nikola Vukovic was mentioned more than once, and I raise that because he is actually mentioned in the witness's statement, but he has more than -- he's also known by another name, et cetera. So he was mentioned in the statement to the investigators in 1998. So unless there's -- he wants to clarify whether every incident Vukovic was mentioned to the investigators, then I think more clarification of the question is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It does say Nikola Vukovic. Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's already up there and --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I withdraw this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. REIDY
utterances.text: -- are the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell me the following: In the statement that you gave in 1998, you did not mention this Russian roulette; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't mention it to this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the statement that you gave to the investigators of the Prosecutor in April of 1998.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you consider that not important enough and that's the reason why you didn't mention it or was there another reason?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it was important for this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you gave the statement based on what this Tribunal would consider important?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "important for this Tribunal," do you mean for the indicted in this case?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, your statement was mainly directed at the behaviour of the accused who are here in Samac in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't speak of some other things that happened there at the time.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were you asked specifically by the OTP investigators about the personalities of the accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you made this statement on your own initiative, knowing who was accused in this case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that is why matters such as this Russian roulette were left out of that statement?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mehinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Mehinovic. I need only to clarify a few points in connection with the period between October and December 1991, and January and April 1992, in Samac. In response to questions put to you by the Prosecution team - that was on Monday - in response to the question by the Prosecution about the exacerbation of interethnic tensions in Samac in the period of March and April 1992, you gave only a partial response. So I would now like to broaden it. Ms. Reidy asked you: [In English], "I'm going to ask you now about the time period 1992, and particularly, March and April 1992. I'd like to know whether you experienced or witnessed an arise in the interethnic tensions in Bosanski Samac in and around this period." Your answer was "Yes." The next question was: "Could you just give us one brief example of how these ethnic tensions showed themselves or manifested themselves?" The answer was: "I don't quite understand. Do you mean before the war, in the month of March?" Then question: "Sorry, Mr. Mehinovic. Yes, exactly, in March, in and around March." And then the answer was: "It was at a time when barricades and roadblocks were put up. We didn't want to have trouble with any political parties. We wanted to continue living together as good friends." [Interpretation] And so on and so forth. Would you please tell the Court now: In the period you are referring to, who was it who set up barricades in Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, these barricades set up in the streets, we used to refer to them as barbecue barricades. All ethnic groups socialised there, and they ate and drank together. They didn't argue among themselves. So all the parties and all the ethnic groups were there, and that's the kind of barricades they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This contradicts your reply about the rising in interethnic tensions, because I think if people go and have barbecues together, this tends to improve interethnic tensions, not to have them deteriorate.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So from this I conclude that your affirmative response to the Prosecution's question as to whether you witnessed any rise in interethnic Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 7624 to 7628. tensions is in fact not yes, but no.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're getting at.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will clarify. When the Prosecutor asked you whether you experienced or witnessed a rise in interethnic tensions in Bosanski Samac in March and April, you answered yes. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but she didn't ask about the barbecue barricades. She asked about the situation in Bosanski Samac, and there already were ethnic tensions. That's what you were supposed to ask me, not about the barricades.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we agree that in late 1991 and early 1992 there was a war in neighbouring Croatia? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we agree on the fact that because of the war, a number of Serbian refugees arrived in Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we agree on the fact that because of the location of Samac, which is only 50 metres away from Croatia, because only the River Sava divides Samac from Croatia, that the influence of the war in Croatia led to heightened tension among the population of Samac in that period?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How did it affect you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it had affected me, I wouldn't have stayed in Samac. I would certainly have left sooner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you and your family were surely upset because of the closeness of war.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course we were upset. Of course we were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I wonder whether you could clarify with the witness concerning what he said on page 45, line 15 to line 19. This was in response to your question as to who set up barricades. So page 45 his answer lines 15 to 19. What I'm wondering is whether he could clarify if these so-called barbecue barricades were places where people of all ethnic groups gathered around to eat, to drink, and so on, what was the purpose of these barricades other than to eat, to drink, to socialise? And secondly, he didn't answer your question directly. Your question on line 13 and 14 was: "Who was it who set up the barricades?" And I don't believe, unless I've missed something, that there was a direct response to that question. So I'd be happy if you could deal with those two things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I will try to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mehinovic, you heard what Her Honour Judge Williams has said. I will ask you: Why did you and your fellow citizens gather at the barricades to socialise and have barbecues?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, parties had been organised, and one had to decide which party to join. A referendum was to be held. That's the referendum that was to show how many members each party had. And then people talked about the parties, discussed them, wondering which one was better. So the citizens decided to have a barbecue barricade to exchange opinions and views about these parties, because we felt better in the former socialist Yugoslavia rather than in the new parties and the new states. I think I've made that clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you please describe to the Court: You were outside on the road. What did these barricades look like physically?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would take out a barbecue, set up a table on the street, and then the first person to bring a table along would put some meat on it. A passerby would come along and they would say, "Please sit down. Help yourself." And then another neighbour would come out and bring out some more food. And that's how the barbecues came about, and these barbecues came to be known as barbecue barricades.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, for example, if a vehicle would try to pass down that street, would it be blocked, would it be stopped, was traffic normal?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, traffic was normal. This was just on the pavements in front of the houses. But the road itself was clear for traffic and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My next question is: Who organised these barricades?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The citizens of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, does that satisfy your inquiry or should I proceed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I think that's fine. If I understand the witness correctly, the word "barricade" therefore in its normal sense as something to block was not the case here. This was simply a social event.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was my understanding too. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mehinovic, would you be so kind as to tell me: I am sure you are aware of certain armed party formations of the Muslim SDA party in Samac, are you not? You've heard of that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An armed party?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about armed units belonging to the party. You heard about that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. When you responded to a question by the Prosecutor on Monday, you mentioned that members of the 4th Detachment carried weapons, and to the Prosecutor's question: "[Previous translation continues]... Samac with these weapons?" Your answer was: "Yes. On numerous occasions they walked with weapons hidden under their jackets. They would move around town and in certain places around the mosque where you could frequently see the SDA." [Interpretation] What I'm interested in is this: You mentioned the SDA, a group of SDA people. Could you explain what that is? What context were you using these words in? What was the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDA was a party, just like the SDS and the HDZ, and you are aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am, and now I want to ask you whether I understand correctly that party gatherings of the SDA were held in a certain part of town near the mosque. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The party gatherings were not held near the mosque. At that time these were held -- what was held there were prayers. That's when people went to the mosque, in the evenings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But why did you mention to the Prosecutor members of the SDA in this context, in what I just read? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose that SDA members frequented the mosque. They went there to learn their prayers and to pray.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I conclude from this, and you will agree with me, that the SDA in Samac was linked to religious institutions, to the Islamic community, was it not?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Did you hear that in Samac the HDZ and the SDA formed certain armed formations in accordance with their party instructions? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about the influx of illegal weapons from Croatia distributed in Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rumours about this went around, but I didn't know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's what I want to know. So there were rumours about it. Would you answer?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mehinovic, would you tell me: Yesterday, in response to certain questions put to you by my colleague about a group of your fellow townspeople - and I will read you a few names - Salko Srna, Mirsad Srna, Hodzic Sabanovic, Dagovic, and so on, do you remember when you were replying yesterday to the question of whether you met these people --?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On page 75, 76, line 1, when my colleague asked you: [In English] "You have already mentioned that they were armed." Your answer was: "Yes."

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You remember that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the persons you met and whom you mentioned during your testimony before this Tribunal and who were armed, were wearing civilian clothes, were they not?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And we will agree that, in essence, these were armed formations in civilian clothing, were they not?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you come across any of the people in these armed formations whom you knew in the SUP or the TO?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only Mirsad Srna.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And we will agree that it is quite logical that he was suspected of belonging to an armed formation and was arrested as such? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there is now speculation on two points. One, Mr. Pantelic had said: Did he come across any of these people in these armed formations. The term "these armed formations" is a wording of counsel. The witness said perhaps. He didn't say that these were armed formations. And secondly he said "We will agree it is quite logical," in other words, asks him to speculate on whether or not other people were suspected by third parties of belonging to armed formations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There is nothing wrong, Ms. Reidy, with this line of questioning, and the answer -- and the witness is quite capable of answering them. So, Mr. Pantelic, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think you have already answered my question, but I will repeat it. We will agree, then, that some of these people, whom you later met in the MUP or the TO, might have been suspected of armed resistance or something like that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but it's possible. Whether they were suspected and whether they actually were that, I don't know. I only know that I saw Mirsad Srna, who was in that group of 20 men, and I don't believe that Mr. Pistoljevic who was over 60 years of age, could have been suspected of being armed.
