Zlatko Stanic, whom everybody knows, I don't believe that he could have been suspected and that he carried weapons because he was a worker and he was the only one who knew how to work with the telephones and the communications equipment in the post office.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If my memory serves me well, you also saw Muhamed Bicic in the TO and the SUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when he was brought from the primary school. It was a day or two or three before the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He was also armed, was he not?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And this also refers to the Dagovic brothers, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about Enes, but not about Safet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You are talking about Esad, not Enes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Esad. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, do you have any personal knowledge of the situation and the position of the Serbs across the River Bosna in the Odzak area in April and May? Did you hear anything about the fate of the Serbs over there?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge or did you hear about certain conflicts after the 15th of April, 1992 in the Odzak and Novi Grad area?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first time I'm hearing of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the period after the 15th of April, 1992, did you hear or know anything about armed conflicts to the south of Samac, in the Gradacac area?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you know anything about armed conflicts and certain tensions after the 15th of April, 1992, in the area of Domaljevac and Orasje?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned of that only after we had been detained in the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So in the period from the 17th of April, 1992 to the 27th of May, 1992, you say that in the surroundings of Samac, everything was peaceful; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There was no shooting?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was on the first day, but not later, or I didn't notice it. There was a little bit of shelling of Samac; I don't know by whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When was Samac shelled?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Wait a minute. I'm a bit confused now. Why would someone be shelling Samac if everything around Samac was peaceful? Would you explain that to the Chamber? It doesn't seem logical to me. Someone is shelling and yet you say the surroundings are peaceful.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, sir, but I am not an expert on war, on military matters, and I cannot say exactly how or why. I don't know. Because the demarcation line was not clear to me. I know that Samac was shelled and the people around Samac were peaceful. And if you know, maybe you can explain it to me, why that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, I will be very direct. I'm putting very simple questions to you. There is nothing for you to conceal.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't try to tell me I'm concealing something or lying. That's not true. And I'm not a military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If there's information you want to put to the witness, you better do so, instead of simply going round and round.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, very simply, Your Honour, I would like to ask him a direct question and he tried to avoid the answer so I will be very precise right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mehinovic, if shells were landing in Samac, does that mean that you are right when you say that everything was Samac was peaceful? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So were these peacemaking shells that were being used?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're asking me superfluous questions. I apologise to the Chamber, but I wouldn't want to continue answering his questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think there's a problem also with the way the questions are put to the witness. The witness has explained that as far as he could see, everybody in Samac, in the place where he was, where he could see, was peaceful. But the shells kept landing on the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My understanding, Your Honour, and my question was whether the surrounding area of Samac was peaceful. That was my question. And I will put it again if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I think he has answered sufficiently on this one, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree. I agree. Because I asked him very simple whether the surrounding area was peaceful, and then it was unlogic to say if it's peaceful, why Samac was shelled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, because he doesn't know who was shelling Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I accept that. But I'm just trying to make this logical connection between two answers, nothing but that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Let's move on to another topic. If you could tell me the following, Mr. Mehinovic: After you were exchanged in 1994 in Sarajevo, did you give any statements about what was happening to you while you were confined? I'm talking about Sarajevo. Maybe you might have talked to some officials.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you give a statement to the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To the UNHCR?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you give any statements to any officials about your confinement to some -- in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I understand you well, you went to the country that you live in now through the UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in this questionnaire that you had to fill in, you did not mention what was happening to you from April 1992 until your release.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I seek clarity on the relevance of this? Because as Defence counsel yesterday pointed this out, there was a time frame put on the questions related to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You will be able to explain that in re-examination, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: At this time, outside of the indictment period, I thought the ruling from the Bench was that Defence counsel in their cross should be discussing only incidents involving the indictment time period. And this transfer to the United States, my understanding is it happened sometime in 1995, which is beyond the indictment period, and it's for that reason that I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, it doesn't mean that no question can be put. He asked in connection with whether or not he did state anything that has happened to him during the time that he was detained. So that's not the time of question that would be disallowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So Mr. Mehinovic, when you came to your current country of residence, did you give any statement there?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: About the events in Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So the first time you talked about these events in Samac in 1998 to the investigators of the Prosecution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, could you bear with me just for a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It is my understanding that I'm finished with my cross-examination. Thank you, Your Honours. [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mehinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, I'd like to discuss with you the record of the interview you had with investigators from the OTP in 1998. In that statement, it said: "Simo Zaric came to me personally with his bodyguard and a police officer." Did you ever say that Simo Zaric actually entered the room in which you were staying?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did Simo Zaric enter the room where you were being detained?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you see Mr. Simo Zaric clearly from where you were being detained?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: In May, in Bosanski Samac, what is the light like in the evening time, when you were being detained, at the time? Was there enough light for you to be able to see Mr. Simo Zaric clearly in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time we didn't need any lights yet. That might have been around 5.00 or 5.30 in the evening, and you could still see very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that "Simo Zaric came to me personally." Are you confident that what you heard -- what you've testified that you heard Simo Zaric say in the corridor and that was directed at you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And why are you so confident about that assertion?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After he left, they came immediately to beat me up, and they didn't move towards anybody else. They just came to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But Simo Zaric didn't come to beat you up, did he?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And are you sure you heard that it was Simo Zaric's voice?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What is it about Simo Zaric's voice that's so distinctive?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He has a very specific voice. It's a little bit coarse, coarser than others.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, I'm just going to ask you about a couple of other things, then, from your statement in -- from the record of this interview in 1998. At that time you told investigators that you had seen Mirsad Jasarevic being beaten by Milan Simic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You also told them at the time that you had witnessed Saban Seric paying Mr. Tadic money?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: This is from your statement. It says: "After my name was removed from the list, Saban Seric paid Tadic 100 Deutschmarks and promised him more money. He got my place in the list and was exchanged." That's what you told investigators in 1998 as well as telling the Tribunal here today, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you tell investigators in 1998 how Miroslav Tadic had come and ordered all the people from Bosanski Samac out of the buses in July, when an exchange was going on?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you also tell investigators in 1998 that Radovan Antic was guarding you when you had to do force the labour in the beginning of the war in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: In your statement, it said that it's recorded as you having said "Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric were personally in charge of the 4th Detachment. Radovan Antic was some kind of deputy commander." Do you recall that now and do you stand by what you said in that statement?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Why do you say that Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric were in charge of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was at Miroslav Tadic's that this was happening, and his names -- and their names were mentioned most closely related to the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you about an issue which arose in the

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic that a police officer had mentioned to you that there would be a Serb -- that you would have a Serb lawyer. Do you remember saying that to Mr. Lukic in response to his question?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Certainly. In your statement -- in the document from 1998, it records you as saying: "I was given a Serb defence lawyer." When Mr. Lukic asked you about that, you said you believed that a policeman may have told you that you would have a Serb defence lawyer. Do you recall that now?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you recall which police officer it was? Maybe not by name, but a police officer whilst you were in the camp, a police officer whilst you were in the jeep, a police officer whilst you were in the courthouse, or some other police officer altogether?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police officer that came to get me in the camp. He was a military police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you arrived at the courthouse, did anyone there ever advise you that you had a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you actually ever meet with a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have any legal counsel or legal advice at any stage during your detention and proceedings in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like now to ask you some questions arising from the cross-examination of Mr. Lazarevic on behalf of Simo Zaric. He asked you about the incident where you gathered in front of the Buducnost factory, and he asked you whether there were Serbs there as well. Can I clarify your answer? The people gathered in front of the Buducnost factory, apart from the soldiers, were they of all ethnic groups or were they only Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were only Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were all the Muslims and Croats wearing white armbands?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were any -- did you see in your time before you were detained any Serb, whether soldier or civilian, walking around Samac with a white armed band?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At this same incident, Mr. Lazarevic suggested that you had been invited to join the 4th Detachment, and I believe you testified that you were not invited to join the 4th Detachment, simply to hand up your reserve uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were a member of the JNA reserve units? You have testified to that. That's correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you went back, as you were required, to refresher courses?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Prior to the breakout of war in Bosanski Samac, were you ever officially invited as a JNA reserve officer to join the ranks of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL MEHINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that's the end of my re-exam. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, being sensitive about the time issue in this trial, I didn't want to raise and interrupt my colleagues, but since like 20 minutes now I don't have a connection with my client on the phone. We don't have any problem to proceed, on the assumption and the hope that he's having, in his room, the -- that he hears what is happening in the trial. If -- I have talked with -- exchanged the messages with the Registry, and if they can confirm that he is having an audio and a video signal in his room, then we are -- I mean, we can proceed without the telephone connection, because I was advised that the technicians are working on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If we can only confirm that, that would be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I confirm that not since the last 20 minutes, but in fact five minutes now that we've been having problems with the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I did confirm with Mr. Tim Mcfadden at the Detention Unit that on their side all is well with the phone. We have the technicians working on the connection from this phone here. At the very moment I'm awaiting a telephone call from them to say that everything has been corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We can proceed. I apologise for this 20 minutes. It appeared to me much longer than it obviously was. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mehinovic. We are through. You have completed your evidence and you may leave courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We were given to understand that the next witness requires protective measures, which were already granted. Is that correct? Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to be asking for additional protective measures. The next witness is already -- actually, could we close the session for this, for the statement, move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 9th day of May, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
